title: workspace-runtime renders authored playbook skills, hook declarations and operation and harness definitions
summary: @inventarch/workspace-runtime's ./internal/generate subpath also exports generatePlaybookSkills(reader, within, host), generateHookSet(reader, within, host), generateHooks(reader, within, host), hookDeclaration(node), HOOK_IDENTITY, HOOK_IDENTITY_LIMIT, registrableHook(identity), registrableSelection(path), HOOK_LIMIT, HOOK_SELECTION_LIMIT, HOOK_SELECTION_LENGTH, generateDefinitions(reader, within, host) and generateHostSet(reader, within, host), with the HookSet and HostSet types. generateHostSet computes everything a host generates once: the agent files then the skills, the hook declarations, every record not rendered or registered, and the definitions, whose harness registrations select only from those files and hooks; generateDefinitions returns its definitions. Each reads only records at band 100 (authored by the workspace) that the scope token admits, by identity; installed and adopted records render nothing and are not reported. generatePlaybookSkills returns a frozen {files, unsupported}: one skill per authored `@playbook` at .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md for claude and .agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md for codex, with the same text (YAML frontmatter with the JSON-quoted name and meaning.says, the packet marker on its own line, the title and identity, then one section per phase in the cycle order orient, plan, act, learn, a phase with no cell left out, the primary primitive's cell first and marked, each cell with its condition's terms and its text written as the position packet writes free text, IA words as code spans, controls and separators as spaces, and `<!--`, a `!` before a rendered code span and a leading `<` escaped); a playbook whose name is not a portable host name, that is named ia-authoring (the packet's own skill), or whose text is not inert prose (judged on each authored cell before rendering, so an unbalanced code span or fence is reported as the cell's own) is an unsupported row {identity, word: 'playbook', reason} and the others still render. generateHookSet returns {hooks, unsupported}: each authored `@hook` that hookDeclaration accepts becomes a HostHookDeclaration {identity, event: 'PreToolUse', tools, paths, message}, which requires event PreToolUse, tools among Write, Edit and MultiEdit (canonical spelling, each once), one to 64 workspace-relative path selections written with / (registrableSelection: none absolute, escaping, longer than 512 characters, holding a . or .. segment or an empty one but the last, or backslashed, and none holding a C0, DEL or C1 control, a bidirectional control or a Unicode line or paragraph separator), a non-blank message and an identity of at most 512 characters; a hook that selects no path is refused rather than registered as a guard that never denies; at most 64 hooks are registered (HOOK_LIMIT), each further one reported; each refused hook is an unsupported row {identity, word: 'hook', reason}, and for codex every authored hook is one. generateHooks returns the accepted declarations. generateDefinitions returns PacketDefinition rows: each authored `@operation` as {name, description, handler, input, output, effects}, a field it does not state absent, and each authored `@harness` as {name, description, workspace, hostProfile, profiles, bindings, registrations}, the registrations being the agent files rendered for its profiles, the skills rendered for the playbooks of their capabilities and included capabilities (none for a profile whose capability closure the composition compiler refuses), and the registered hooks its bindings target, as identities and paths; a record the host does not render or register selects nothing, so hook or agent support never fails the definitions. An unknown host is refused with IA-PROJECTION-INPUT-INVALID, and an unknown or stale scope token keeps its database code. Limits: the generator copies an operation's handler and input/output ids as authored catalog keys; generation never imports, resolves, serves or executes them. The separate local runner host executes its fixed installed captured-read operation under the selected mandate and bounded runtime, and the MCP door serves no new tool; tool values are never read as a regex or shell text.
